h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, ו׳ Ki Seitzei, 6
The New Face of the Additional Shabbos Soul

p: HaKadosh Baruch Hu gives a person
so why did the Gemara call it
since from it the nefesh was lost";
which has lost what it lost:
it has lost that crown, etc."
But from the Gemara it appears
that the additional nefesh is lost
and this is the Shabbos day,
for there is the union of the Shechinah
'That gives its fruit in its season'
this is the season of the tzaddik,
in a person there are three levels:
and the three days before Shabbos:
that on the fourth day there shines
the aspect of the additional nefesh
and on the fifth day there shines
for the three days after Shabbos.
the nefesh, which is the blood,
And the neshamah is in the brain,
all of nefesh, ruach and neshamah
For the nefesh, which is in action:
it is as if there came into his hand
and he was saved from it,
like one who performs a mitzvah,
"That your speech on Shabbos not be
like your speech on a weekday";
to deduce from what is written,
that on Shabbos one should speak,
only that it should be "a word,"
and this is the aspect of ruach,
come from the side of the person:
and through the change in speech,
comes from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
that he should have on Shabbos
And this is what was precisely stated
HaKadosh Baruch Hu gives a person
for this HaKadosh Baruch Hu gives.

p: which is the power of action,
and it is understandable that it is called
and so too the aspect of ruach,
which is also recognizable on Shabbos,
in that one's speech is different,
for one speaks only words of Torah
which is not so of the additional neshamah,
in the brain and the heart
that it should be called "new faces"?
for wisdom that is in the brain
is recognizable on the face as well.
"A glad heart makes a good countenance,"
and it is recognizable on the face.
And this is what is said
since Shabbos counts as new faces
although it is in the heart,
is also recognizable on the face,
and one who has no shamefacedness,
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds,
he is ashamed to do anything
against the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
And so it says in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 7):
"The awe of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz";
and all of Yisrael are called
and it is recognizable on the face as well,
And this is what is said:
for this is recognizable to all,
that they are new on Shabbos,
And as for what appears here
of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah
through the mitzvah of keeping Shabbos,
as is written in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 6):
HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah,
and cause them to be joined together,
they inherit from there souls, etc."
of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah."
And so, right at the entry of Shabbos,
which is at the time of the addition to Shabbos
the unification of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah.
and the unification and union take place,
And this is what the Gemara says:
HaKadosh Baruch Hu gives a person
that is, at the time of the addition to Shabbos,
